newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy state spending on advertising seen up in '97.
newsitem.headline: Italy state spending on advertising seen up in '97.

text.p: Spending by Italian ministries on advertising and publicity campaigns is seen rising this year but remains well below that spent in Britain and Germany, the Italian association of advertising agencies (Assap) said.
Assap said the Italian state planned to invest a total of between 450 and 500 billion lire ($260-290 million) in 1997 for public communication.
While this was well up on the 223 billion lire Italian ministries spent last year, Britain spent 10 times as much and Germany at least five times as much, the Association said.

Assap gave the figures at a news conference to present a new self-regulatory code for the advertising industry aimed to increase transparency when participating in invitations to tender for both state and private contracts.

Assap chairman Alberto Contri said the recommendations had received the approval of Italy's Antitrust authority which had in the past been critical of certain ethical norms which could have been seen as restricting free competition.
He said the new norms would make tender procedures more efficient, competitive and more professional particularly in the public sector where in the past "a lot was left to be desired."

He did not go into specific details but said the recommendations were aimed at improving aspects such as over-long product delivery times, too many agencies being invited to tender for contracts and tenders being awarded on unclear criteria.
